allVisibleCapturedMeaning: true = every quest VISIBLE to this profile was captured, completed, active, failed, or listed-but-locked, across every tab the trader shows. It does NOT mean every quest the trader has: anything still gated behind an unfinished quest or an unreached loyalty level is not on screen and is therefore not here. No trader in this collection is complete in the absolute sense.
allVisibleCapturedNote: LL1-LL4 plus the essential group were all sent.

profile.note: Confirmed PvE on 2026-08-10; see the Fence batch, whose [PVE ZONE] cards carry ids that exist only in tarkov.dev's pve task list.
profile.factionNote: USEC. DETERMINED FROM THE COLLECTION ITSELF, not something written down at capture time. Four quests are faction-exclusive with no counterpart id: Road Closed (USEC), Green Corridor (BEAR), Our Own Land (BEAR) and Counteraction (USEC). "Road Closed" is ACTIVE on this profile, and the wiki says outright that it is "only obtainable by USEC PMCs" with Green Corridor as its BEAR counterpart. Both BEAR-only quests are absent from Prapor's list, which was captured in full. A BEAR profile could not show Road Closed and would have to show the other two, so the reading is unambiguous.

reading: Read off the in-game quest screen. Objective text is verbatim, including the (Optional) prefix.

quests.name: The Huntsman Path - Administrator
quests.itemChanged:
THREE SOURCES, THREE DIFFERENT MAPS, and the game wins. The map is LIGHTHOUSE, launch a yellow signal flare at the train station. Confirmed in game on 2026-08-11. tarkov.dev says Streets of Tarkov; the wiki says Reserve ("Shoot a yellow signal flare in the Train depot", "Eliminate any target in the train depot on reserve"). Both are wrong, and this is the only quest in the collection where all three sources name a different map.
  The wiki's claim was invisible until the map scan was made case-insensitive: it writes "on reserve" in lowercase, so a case-sensitive scan found no map at all and graded the wiki `silent`.

quests.name: The Tarkov Shooter - Part 4
quests.lineShattered:
THE LINE IS STABLE FOR THREE PARTS AND THEN THE SOURCE HAS TWO EXTRA, the second renumbering found, after The Punisher. Read off the full source line:
  game 1,2,3 = source 1,2,3, word for word (only 'while using' became 'with').
  game 4 'Eliminate any target with a bolt-action rifle' matches NO source part; source 4 is 'PMC operatives from over 80 meters away' and source 5 is 'Scavs 21:00-05:00 on Customs'. Both of those are gone from the game.
  game 5 = source 6 (Sniper Scavs). game 6 = source 7 (suppressed).
  So the game dropped two mid-line parts and renumbered the rest down by one. The wiki has partly followed: it titles source Part 8's page 'The Tarkov Shooter - Part 7'.
  THE DETECTOR'S FLAG WAS RIGHT AND ITS SUGGESTION WAS WRONG. It proposed source Part 8 for game Part 6 (53% word overlap vs 36%), but the correct answer is Part 7, the distinctive token 'suppressed' is worth less to a Jaccard score than the filler words 'with' and 'a' that Part 8 happens to share. Trust the flag, verify the suggestion by reading the text. Third time a similarity heuristic has named the wrong quest while correctly noticing something was off.
objectives: Eliminate any target with a bolt-action rifle (15)
quests.openQuestion: THE ONLY PART OF THIS LINE CONTENT CANNOT PIN. Every other part matches a tarkov.dev record word for word once the renumbering is undone, but this card reads "Eliminate any target with a bolt-action rifle (15)" and NO source has that objective. tarkov.dev's Part 4 and the wiki's Part 4 both say "5 PMC operatives from over 80 meters away". By position it should be tarkov.dev id 5bc480a686f7741af0342e29, and the wiki is otherwise exactly right about this line, it renumbered 5, 6 and 7 to match the game and deleted the old Part 5 (night kills on Customs), which no longer exists anywhere. So either the wiki has not updated this one page's objective text, or the reading needs a second look. Left unpinned rather than guessed.
